summary: Dara Sakor International Airport serves the remote southwestern coast of Cambodia in Koh Kong Province, near the developed Dara Sakor resort zone. The facility features one of the longest runways in Cambodia, built to accommodate long-haul wide-body aircraft as part of a large-scale regional development initiative. Commercial passenger traffic remains limited, with service primarily tied to charter and seasonal routes linked to coastal tourism and investment-related travel.
faqs:
Q: Where is Dara Sakor International Airport located?
A: The airport is in Ta Noun commune, Koh Kong Province, in southwestern Cambodia, near the coast and the Dara Sakor development zone.

Q: What airlines currently fly into DSY?
A: Scheduled commercial service has been historically limited, with operations varying over time. Travelers should check current route availability closer to their travel date.

Q: How large is Dara Sakor Airport compared to other Cambodian airports?
A: The airport was built to large-airport standards with an extended runway suitable for wide-body jets, making it one of the more spacious airfields in the country even though passenger volumes remain modest.

Q: Is the airport near any major tourist attractions?
A: Yes, it provides access to the Dara Sakor coastal area, Botum Sakor National Park, and beach destinations along the Gulf of Thailand coast.
transport_tips: Ground transport options at DSY are limited due to the small volume of commercial flights, so arranging a private transfer or hotel pickup in advance is strongly recommended. The airport is roughly a 4-5 hour drive from Phnom Penh and a shorter drive from the Thai border at Hat Lek. Taxi apps and ride services are generally not available in this remote area, so plan transportation before arrival.
local_tip: Cell phone coverage and mobile data can be unreliable in the surrounding Koh Kong coast, so download offline maps and confirm your transfer details with your hotel before leaving the airport terminal.
